static_traits.name: Li Yifan
static_traits.family_status: Close relationship with the older sister, travels to Canada every autumn to visit; other family circumstances not mentioned
static_traits.social_status: Relationships with colleagues are affected, avoids social gatherings involving driving; other social situations not mentioned
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; no prior history of similar problems; has not received psychotherapy
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, relatively strong logic, high cooperation, sincere tone; but has evident anxiety and a tendency toward self-deprecating labeling

basic_info.main_problem: Because of my daily subway commute, I have developed and solidified the belief 'I will always be a failure and will never be able to drive,' leading to persistent anxiety and inferiority, affecting my work performance, social life, and daily travel planning.
basic_info.core_demands: This belief affects my daily life and causes distress, and I find it hard to resolve alone, so I seek counseling to challenge and change these negative thoughts.
growth_experiences: About a year ago, the client encountered difficulties while learning to drive; the stress was great, and the client felt they must obtain a driver's license as soon as possible; after the driving lessons went poorly, the client began to form beliefs such as 'taking the subway = failure' and 'I will never learn to drive', which gradually escalated into avoiding further driving lessons, accompanied by anxiety and inferiority.

core_beliefs: I will never learn to drive

special_situations.event: Seeing colleagues drive into the company parking lot
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot drive myself to work, it means I am unsuccessful, I am a failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoiding continuing to learn to drive, reducing participation in social activities involving driving
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I can never succeed; I am just a failure

special_situations.event: Needing to plan travel methods and transport arrangements
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I rely on public transport, it means I am not independent, not competent
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Goes out less or chooses to avoid activities requiring driving, to reduce the risk of being compared and evaluated
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Taking the subway to work shows I am inferior

special_situations.event: Recalling or facing past setbacks when learning to drive
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If learning to drive does not go smoothly, it proves I am no good and will not succeed in the future either
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Stopped trying to learn to drive, instead reading self-help articles or chatting generally with friends to seek comfort but no longer taking action
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I cannot do it; I will never learn to drive

special_situations.event: On the road, seeing others drive (including strangers)
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If others can drive and I cannot, I am worse than others and of lower worth
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Labels the self a 'failure' and withdraws, avoiding driving-related interactions or topics
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am not as good as them; I do not deserve to join these activities

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be seen as independent, competent, and valuable (able to control transport, gain social recognition)
core_conflict.fear: Fears failure and humiliation, being looked down on by others and labeled a 'failure'
defense_goal: Reducing possible failure and shame by avoiding learning to drive and using self-deprecating labels
Keeps troubles hidden, not revealing them to close people (such as an older sister), to avoid judgment and exposing vulnerability

object_relations.object_representation: The successful driver / potential judge (others may look down on me)

manifestations: Regards 'being able to drive' as a symbol of independence and control, and interprets 'taking the subway' as lacking autonomy and being passively dependent
Facing the current inability to drive produces strong questioning of self-worth and existential anxiety
outcomes: Avoids learning to drive and related socializing
Declining work performance and increased daily travel stress

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'. Language manifestations include: 'I must/should...', 'Everyone is like this', and so on.
manifestations: Takes 'only being able to drive counts as success' as an absolute standard and internalizes it as a rule of self-evaluation
Measuring self-worth by whether one drives, ignoring other aspects of success

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains the impulse to act toward other people or objects, or gives up seeking others to do something for them and instead does it to themselves; that is, the individual redirects energy originally intended outward toward themselves, corresponding to 'impulse'. Language manifestations include: 'Forget it, I will just endure it', 'I should not trouble others', and so on
manifestations: Has not told the older sister or support system about the specific troubles, internalizing the stress and shame and bearing them alone
In situations requiring driving, chooses withdrawal and self-reproach rather than seeking help outwardly

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'. Language manifestations include: 'It is all my fault that he was hurt', 'I do not deserve to talk to him', and so on
manifestations: Repeatedly labeling oneself a 'failure' and judging oneself harshly
Excessively worries about others' views in social and work settings, withdrawing due to self-reproach

positive_force: Close relationship with the older sister; a potential support resource is available
Having ability and sense of responsibility at work, having successful experience as counter-evidence
Clear motivation to seek help, positive attitude, willing to try reality testing and restructuring thinking
negative_force: Catastrophizing and overgeneralization, equating a single ability (driving) with overall self-worth
Labeling oneself a 'failure', reinforcing shame and inferiority
Avoiding learning to drive and social activities involving driving, maintaining the problem cycle
Makes negative predictions about the future (will never learn it / will never succeed), reducing willingness to try
Seeing others drive or planning transport triggers strong anxiety and physical reactions, weakening functional performance

target_behavior.behavior: Avoids learning to drive and social activities involving driving
antecedent: Encountering difficulties when learning to drive
Seeing that an activity requires driving, or colleagues driving in
Needing to plan transportation for travel
target_behavior.core_reason: Strictly binds driving with self-worth, showing catastrophizing and overgeneralization (not being able to drive = a failure), and chooses avoidance to avoid failure and shame
target_behavior.function: Escaping possible failure and judgment for short-term relief of anxiety
target_behavior.consequence: Work performance is affected, self-confidence declines, socializing decreases, and daily travel planning becomes a source of stress

target_behavior.behavior: When seeing others drive or planning transportation, strong anxiety and self-deprecating automatic thoughts and physiological reactions appear (increased heart rate, chest tightness, low mood)
antecedent: Needing to plan transport or talking about driver's license/driving topics
target_behavior.core_reason: Engages in emotional reasoning and negative prediction about the symbolic meaning of driving ('I will never learn it / I am a failure'), and uses this to confirm the self-label
target_behavior.function: Through self-deprecation and negative expectations, 'reminds' themselves to avoid trying, lowering in the short term the anxiety triggered by uncertainty
target_behavior.consequence: Marked psychological distress and emotional exhaustion, leading to declined work performance, social withdrawal, and impaired overall quality of life
